title: L003: Wire MultiReporter in up.go with integration tests
description:
**Size:** 📦 medium
**Category:** backend
**Priority:** high
**Source:** Proposed for 'It should be possible in Metrics, Log Forwarding u'

Wire the MultiReporter into the main application startup in `up.go`: when `cfg.<Pipeline>.LocalEndpoint.URL` is non-empty, construct a `LocalReporter` with the configured URL and secret key, then wrap `[platformReporter, localReporter]` into a `MultiReporter` before passing to the pipeline's constructor. When URL is empty, behavior is unchanged (platform-only reporter). Add integration/E2E tests that spin up a mock local HTTP server alongside the platform mock, configure dual delivery, and verify both targets receive the correct JSON batches. Test error scenarios: local endpoint down (platform still receives data), invalid credentials, TLS skip-verify behavior.

**Rationale:** Connects L001 config and L002 reporters into the running application. Integration tests validate the full path from config parsing through credential resolution to dual HTTP delivery, catching wiring bugs that unit tests miss. This is where the feature becomes functional end-to-end.

**Affected Areas:**
- src/cmd/up.go
- src/internal/metrics/metrics.go
- src/internal/logfwd/logfwd.go
- src/internal/auditfwd/auditfwd.go
- src/tests/integration/local_endpoint_test.go

stories.title: Platform receives data when local endpoint is not configured
stories.want: the three observability pipelines (metrics, logs, audit) to continue delivering data exclusively to the platform when no local endpoint URL is configured
stories.so_that: existing deployments with no local_endpoint config are unaffected by the MultiReporter wiring
criteria: When cfg.Metrics.LocalEndpoint.URL is empty, the Manager receives the raw ControlPlane client (not a MultiReporter)
When cfg.LogFwd.LocalEndpoint.URL is empty, the Forwarder receives the raw ControlPlane client
When cfg.AuditFwd.LocalEndpoint.URL is empty, the Forwarder receives the raw ControlPlane client
No SecretFetcher calls are made when local endpoints are unconfigured

stories.title: Both platform and local endpoint receive identical batches
stories.want: metrics, logs, and audit data to be delivered to both the platform and my local endpoint simultaneously when local_endpoint.url is configured
stories.so_that: I can ingest observability data into my own monitoring stack alongside the Plexsphere platform
criteria: The platform mock and the local mock HTTP server both receive the same JSON batch body
Both targets receive the correct Authorization header (platform: node secret key, local: bearer token from SecretFetcher)
Delivery to both targets happens concurrently (not sequentially)
The log message 'local endpoint enabled' is emitted with pipeline name and URL for each configured pipeline

stories.title: Platform delivery continues when local endpoint is down
stories.want: platform delivery to succeed even when my local endpoint is unreachable or returns errors
stories.so_that: a local infrastructure failure does not degrade my platform monitoring
criteria: When local endpoint returns HTTP 500, platform still receives the batch successfully
When local endpoint is unreachable (connection refused), platform delivery is unaffected
Local endpoint errors are logged at WARN level with component name
The return value of ReportMetrics/ReportLogs/ReportAudit is the platform error (nil when platform succeeds)

stories.title: Local endpoint receives bearer token from credential resolution
stories.want: the local endpoint to be authenticated with a bearer token resolved from the platform secret store
stories.so_that: my local endpoint is securely authenticated using the existing secret delivery mechanism
criteria: LocalReporter calls SecretFetcher.FetchSecret with the configured secret_key name
The resolved token is sent as 'Authorization: Bearer {token}' header
Token is cached and reused within the 5-minute TTL
When SecretFetcher fails but a stale token exists, the stale token is used with a warning log

stories.title: TLS skip-verify is respected for local endpoints
stories.want: to be able to configure tls_insecure_skip_verify for local endpoints using self-signed certificates
stories.so_that: I can use internal CA certificates or self-signed certs in development without TLS errors
criteria: When tls_insecure_skip_verify is true, LocalReporter connects to endpoints with self-signed TLS certs without error
When tls_insecure_skip_verify is false (default), self-signed cert endpoints cause a TLS error
The TLS configuration only affects the local endpoint's HTTP client, not the platform client

stories.title: Invalid credential causes local delivery failure without affecting platform
stories.want: the system to gracefully handle credential resolution failures for local endpoints
stories.so_that: a misconfigured secret_key does not prevent platform data delivery
criteria: When FetchSecret returns an error and no cached token exists, the local reporter returns an error
The MultiReporter logs the local error as a warning but returns nil if platform succeeded
Platform data delivery is not blocked by credential resolution for local endpoint
Error messages include the pipeline component name for troubleshooting

stories.title: Integration test validates end-to-end dual delivery for all three pipelines
stories.want: integration tests that exercise the full path from config parsing through MultiReporter wiring to dual HTTP delivery
stories.so_that: wiring bugs in up.go that unit tests cannot catch are detected before release
criteria: Tests spin up mock HTTP servers for both platform and local endpoints
Tests configure the pipeline with LocalEndpoint.URL pointing to the mock local server
Tests verify that both servers receive the correct JSON payloads
Tests cover all three pipelines: metrics, logfwd, auditfwd

requirements.description: The system SHALL construct a MultiReporter wrapping platform and local reporters when cfg.<Pipeline>.LocalEndpoint.URL is non-empty
requirements.rationale: Core wiring logic that enables dual-destination delivery

scenarios.name: Metrics MultiReporter wired when URL configured
scenarios.when: cfg.Metrics.LocalEndpoint.URL is 'https://metrics.local:9090/ingest'
scenarios.then: the Manager receives a MultiReporter that dispatches to both ControlPlane and LocalReporter
and_then: logger.Info is called with pipeline=metrics and the configured URL

scenarios.name: LogFwd MultiReporter wired when URL configured
scenarios.when: cfg.LogFwd.LocalEndpoint.URL is 'https://logs.local:9090/ingest'
scenarios.then: the Forwarder receives a MultiReporter that dispatches to both ControlPlane and LocalReporter
and_then: logger.Info is called with pipeline=logfwd and the configured URL

scenarios.name: AuditFwd MultiReporter wired when URL configured
scenarios.when: cfg.AuditFwd.LocalEndpoint.URL is 'https://audit.local:9090/ingest'
scenarios.then: the Forwarder receives a MultiReporter that dispatches to both ControlPlane and LocalReporter
and_then: logger.Info is called with pipeline=auditfwd and the configured URL

requirements.description: The system SHALL pass the platform reporter directly (not MultiReporter) when cfg.<Pipeline>.LocalEndpoint.URL is empty
requirements.rationale: Zero-overhead when local endpoints are not configured

scenarios.name: Empty URL uses platform-only reporter
scenarios.when: cfg.Metrics.LocalEndpoint.URL is empty
scenarios.then: the Manager receives the ControlPlane client directly as its MetricsReporter
and_then: no 'local endpoint enabled' log message is emitted

scenarios.name: Zero-valued LocalEndpointConfig uses platform-only reporter
scenarios.when: cfg.LogFwd.LocalEndpoint is a zero-valued struct
scenarios.then: the Forwarder receives the ControlPlane client directly as its LogReporter
and_then: no LocalReporter is constructed

scenarios.name: All pipelines independent
scenarios.when: only cfg.Metrics.LocalEndpoint.URL is configured, logfwd and auditfwd are empty
scenarios.then: only the metrics pipeline uses MultiReporter; logfwd and auditfwd use platform-only
and_then: each pipeline is independently configurable

requirements.description: The system SHALL deliver identical JSON batches to both platform and local endpoints concurrently
requirements.rationale: The local endpoint must receive the exact same payload as the platform for data consistency

scenarios.name: Both targets receive same metrics batch
scenarios.when: the metrics Manager flushes a batch of 3 MetricPoints
scenarios.then: both the platform and local HTTP servers receive a POST with the same 3-element JSON array
and_then: Content-Type is application/json on both requests

scenarios.name: Both targets receive same log batch
scenarios.when: the log Forwarder flushes a batch of 5 LogEntries
scenarios.then: both platform and local receive POST requests with identical 5-element JSON arrays

scenarios.name: Both targets receive same audit batch
scenarios.when: the audit Forwarder flushes a batch of 2 AuditEntries
scenarios.then: both platform and local receive POST requests with identical 2-element JSON arrays

requirements.description: The system SHALL continue platform delivery when the local endpoint fails
requirements.rationale: Local endpoint failures must never degrade platform data delivery

scenarios.name: Local endpoint returns HTTP 500
scenarios.when: the local endpoint returns HTTP 500 for a metrics batch
scenarios.then: ReportMetrics returns nil (platform succeeded) and logs a warning about local failure
and_then: the platform received the batch successfully

scenarios.name: Local endpoint connection refused
scenarios.when: the local endpoint is unreachable (connection refused)
scenarios.then: ReportMetrics returns nil (platform succeeded) and logs a warning
and_then: no retry is attempted for the local endpoint

scenarios.name: Local endpoint slow does not block platform
scenarios.when: the local endpoint takes 5 seconds to respond but platform responds in 10ms
scenarios.then: MultiReporter still waits for both but returns the platform result
and_then: total time is bounded by the slower endpoint

requirements.description: The system SHALL authenticate local endpoint requests with a bearer token resolved from SecretFetcher
requirements.rationale: Credentials are resolved through the existing encrypted secret delivery pipeline for security

scenarios.name: Bearer token in Authorization header
scenarios.when: LocalReporter sends a POST to the local endpoint
scenarios.then: the request includes 'Authorization: Bearer {decrypted_token}' header
and_then: the token was obtained via FetchSecret + DecryptSecret

scenarios.name: Credential resolution failure with no cache
scenarios.when: FetchSecret returns an error and no cached token exists
scenarios.then: LocalReporter returns an error and no HTTP POST is made
and_then: MultiReporter logs the error and returns nil if platform succeeded

scenarios.name: Stale cache used on fetch failure
scenarios.when: FetchSecret fails but a previous token is cached (expired TTL)
scenarios.then: the stale cached token is used and a warning is logged
and_then: the HTTP POST is made with the stale token

requirements.description: The system SHALL respect tls_insecure_skip_verify for local endpoint connections
requirements.rationale: Operators may use self-signed certificates for internal local endpoints

scenarios.name: Skip verify allows self-signed certs
scenarios.when: tls_insecure_skip_verify is true and the local endpoint has a self-signed TLS certificate
scenarios.then: the HTTP POST succeeds without TLS verification errors

scenarios.name: Default verify rejects self-signed certs
scenarios.when: tls_insecure_skip_verify is false and the local endpoint has a self-signed certificate
scenarios.then: the HTTP POST fails with a TLS certificate verification error
and_then: the error is logged as a warning by MultiReporter

scenarios.name: TLS settings are per-client
scenarios.when: tls_insecure_skip_verify is true for the local endpoint
scenarios.then: only the LocalReporter's HTTP client has InsecureSkipVerify=true
and_then: the platform client's TLS settings are unaffected

requirements.description: The system SHALL construct LocalReporter with the correct parameters from config and runtime identity
requirements.rationale: Wiring correctness: LocalReporter must receive the endpoint config, the ControlPlane as SecretFetcher, the NSK bytes, and the node ID

scenarios.name: LocalReporter receives correct config
scenarios.when: cfg.Metrics.LocalEndpoint has URL, SecretKey, and TLSInsecureSkipVerify set
scenarios.then: NewLocalReporter is called with that config, the ControlPlane client as fetcher, identity NSK, and identity NodeID

scenarios.name: NSK bytes passed correctly
scenarios.when: the node secret key is used for LocalReporter construction
scenarios.then: []byte(identity.NodeSecretKey) is passed as the nsk parameter
and_then: the same NSK is used for DecryptSecret to resolve bearer tokens

scenarios.name: Each pipeline gets its own LocalReporter
scenarios.when: all three pipelines have local endpoints configured
scenarios.then: three separate LocalReporter instances are created, each with its pipeline-specific config
and_then: each LocalReporter has its own HTTP client and credential cache

requirements.description: Integration tests SHALL validate end-to-end dual delivery including credential resolution
requirements.rationale: Integration tests catch wiring bugs that unit tests miss

scenarios.name: Metrics dual delivery E2E
scenarios.when: a metrics Manager is configured with a LocalEndpoint pointing to a mock HTTPS server
scenarios.then: both the platform mock and the local mock receive the same metric batch via HTTP POST
and_then: the local server receives a valid Authorization: Bearer header

scenarios.name: LogFwd dual delivery E2E
scenarios.when: a log Forwarder is configured with a LocalEndpoint pointing to a mock HTTPS server
scenarios.then: both platform and local mocks receive the same log batch
and_then: batches are JSON-decoded and field counts match

scenarios.name: AuditFwd dual delivery E2E
scenarios.when: an audit Forwarder is configured with a LocalEndpoint pointing to a mock HTTPS server
scenarios.then: both platform and local mocks receive the same audit batch
and_then: each mock server received exactly one POST request

requirements.description: Integration tests SHALL verify error isolation when local endpoint fails
requirements.rationale: Error isolation is the most critical behavioral guarantee

scenarios.name: Local endpoint down, platform receives data
scenarios.when: the local endpoint mock is stopped during a metrics flush
scenarios.then: the platform mock still receives the metric batch and the Manager does not retry
and_then: a warning log is emitted about the local failure

scenarios.name: Local endpoint returns 401, platform unaffected
scenarios.when: the local endpoint returns HTTP 401 Unauthorized
scenarios.then: the platform mock receives the batch, and a warning is logged about the 401

scenarios.name: Local credential resolution fails
scenarios.when: the SecretFetcher returns an error for the local endpoint credential
scenarios.then: the platform mock still receives the batch
and_then: a warning log mentions the credential resolution failure

requirements.description: Integration tests SHALL verify TLS skip-verify behavior end-to-end
requirements.rationale: TLS configuration must be verified in an integration context with real TLS servers

scenarios.name: Skip-verify succeeds against self-signed server
scenarios.when: a LocalReporter is configured with tls_insecure_skip_verify=true against an httptest.NewTLSServer
scenarios.then: the POST request succeeds and the local server receives the batch

scenarios.name: Strict verify fails against self-signed server
scenarios.when: a LocalReporter is configured with tls_insecure_skip_verify=false against an httptest.NewTLSServer
scenarios.then: the POST request fails with a TLS error
and_then: platform delivery is unaffected

review_criteria: All integration tests pass with `go test -race ./internal/metrics/ ./internal/logfwd/ ./internal/auditfwd/` — no data races
Each pipeline (metrics, logfwd, auditfwd) has integration tests covering: dual delivery happy path, local endpoint failure isolation, credential resolution failure, TLS skip-verify
Integration tests use httptest.NewTLSServer for realistic TLS behavior and verify actual HTTP requests (method, headers, body)
Integration tests verify identical JSON payloads delivered to both platform and local endpoints by deserializing and comparing batch element counts
Error isolation verified: platform receives data in all local-failure scenarios (connection refused, HTTP 500, credential failure)
No modifications to production code (up.go wiring is already implemented) — this feature is integration-test-only
Tests follow existing conventions: table-driven where appropriate, discardLogger helper, testNSK/encryptTestSecret helpers reused from local_reporter_test.go
Test file naming follows project convention: integration_test.go in each pipeline package
implementation_notes:
CRITICAL FINDING: The MultiReporter wiring in up.go (lines 480-515) is ALREADY IMPLEMENTED for all three pipelines. The code currently:

1. metrics (lines 480-486): `var metricsReporter metrics.MetricsReporter = client; if cfg.Metrics.LocalEndpoint.URL != "" { localMetrics := metrics.NewLocalReporter(...); metricsReporter = metrics.NewMultiReporter(client, localMetrics, logger) }`
2. logfwd (lines 497-502): Same pattern with `logfwd.NewLocalReporter → logfwd.NewMultiReporter`
3. auditfwd (lines 509-514): Same pattern with `auditfwd.NewLocalReporter → auditfwd.NewMultiReporter`

All three pass `client` (ControlPlane) as the SecretFetcher, `nsk` ([]byte of identity.NodeSecretKey) as the NSK, and `identity.NodeID` as the node ID.

Therefore, this feature (L003) is entirely about INTEGRATION TESTS that validate the full end-to-end path from config parsing through credential resolution to dual HTTP delivery. No production code changes are needed.

Key architectural decisions:
- Integration tests should be in each pipeline's package (internal tests) to access internal types and helpers
- Tests should use httptest.NewTLSServer for both platform and local mocks to exercise real HTTP/TLS
- The mockSecretFetcher from local_reporter_test.go can be reused (it's package-internal)
- Tests should run the full Manager/Forwarder.Run loop with short intervals rather than calling ReportMetrics directly, to validate the complete flush path
- The conditional wiring pattern (platform-only vs MultiReporter) should be tested explicitly

Risks:
- Integration tests with real HTTP servers and tickers need careful timeout management to avoid flaky tests
- Tests must use `go test -race` to catch any concurrency issues in the MultiReporter fan-out
- httptest.NewTLSServer uses self-signed certs, which is perfect for testing TLS skip-verify behavior
